paras: The Pocahontas police shooting and clash of 1888 began when a policeman at Pocahontas shot and killed a Black man on the night of Saturday, November 17, 1888, while, by the report, the man was resisting arrest. Three nights later a large crowd of Black residents tried to lynch the policeman, and in the fight that followed one Black man was killed and several were wounded. The only report found, a Lynchburg telegram printed in the Richmond Dispatch, described it as another clash between the races at Pocahontas.
The telegram called the trouble "another clash between whites and blacks at Pocahontas," which suggests earlier conflict in the town, though it gave no details of any earlier incident.

On Saturday night, November 17, an unnamed policeman shot and killed a man the report called "a negro" who, it said, "was resisting arrest." The report did not say why the man was being arrested, and it gave the officer's justification without attribution. On the night of November 20, according to the telegram dated the next day, "a large crowd of negroes endeavored to lynch the policeman who did the shooting." A fight ensued in which one Black man was killed and several were wounded; the report did not say who fired or whether the policeman was hurt.

The telegram closed by noting that "a great deal of excitement exists." No names of the policeman or of the dead and wounded appear in the coverage, and no report of an inquest, arrest or trial was found.

The Richmond Dispatch ran the news on November 22 as three sentences at the end of "Hill City's Budget," a column of Lynchburg items under the subhead "Trouble at Pocahontas," after notes on a planned belt railroad and the death of a local merchant. The story reached Richmond second-hand, as "a dispatch" received in Lynchburg, and it used the word "negro" throughout while naming no one. It framed the deaths as a racial "clash" and accepted the resisting-arrest account of the first killing without comment.

The report names only Pocahontas; county and state are not stated
An unnamed policeman for the first killing; the killers in the fight are not named
The report describes an attempted lynching of the policeman by a Black crowd, which failed; the killings were by a policeman and in the fight
